clue.text: 14 down goes round Icelandic capital — a small city where people walk up and down

definitions.text: where people walk up and down

indicators.note: goes round says the star piece encloses the next letter

parts.note: the answer to 14 down is a leading man, i.e. a star of the show

indicators.note: capital means the first letter of Icelandic

parts.note: Wells in Somerset is England's smallest city

explanation.surface: A celebrity circles Reykjavik before heading to a little cathedral city full of strollers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Icelandic capital' looks like Reykjavik, but it is only the first letter, which 'goes round' encloses. Wells, in Somerset, is England's smallest cathedral city.
explanation.definitionFit: Stairwells are the shafts housing staircases, where people climb and descend.

clue.text: Animals with peculiar prehensile tails, certainly not quite right

indicators.note: tails means the final letters of peculiar and prehensile
not quite means the last letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: indeed is an emphatic yes, certainly

explanation.surface: Some creatures with odd grasping tails are surely not quite right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prehensile tails' suggests monkeys, but 'tails' just takes the last letters R and E; 'not quite' cuts INDEED to INDEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Reindeer are a species of deer, so they are animals by example.

clue.text: Rather balmy, somewhat like Basil?

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone called Basil is described as a bit mad.
explanation.walkthrough: Basil looks like a person's name (Basil Fawlty comes to mind) but here it is the plant, signalled by the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Basil is a culinary plant, so something like it is herbal in nature.

clue.text: A nobody taking out old queen

indicators.note: taking out signals that the following letter is removed from the synonym

parts.note: none means no one, nobody

explanation.surface: A nonentity is escorting an elderly monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking out' reads like escorting someone on a date, but it signals removal of O from NONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Anne was Queen of Great Britain from 1702 to 1714, an example of a queen.

clue.text: No fab clues — as an anagram is apt to be misleading

indicators.note: as an anagram says the preceding words are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A setter boasts that these aren't clever clues, since anagrams can confuse.
explanation.definitionFit: Something confusable is liable to be mistaken for something else, hence misleading.

clue.text: One on a mission is less refined about 21 across, we hear

indicators.note: about says the cruder piece goes round the sounded letters

parts.note: cruder means less refined

indicators.note: we hear says the cross-referenced word is taken by its sound

parts.note: the answer to 21 across is a written piece, pronounced like the letters S and A

explanation.surface: A missionary is rougher around the edges in his writing, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: The 21 across answer, said out loud, is two letter names, S A; these go inside CRUDER.
explanation.definitionFit: A crusader campaigns zealously for a cause, someone with a mission.

clue.text: Grievance of Protestant leader with post-Reformation Latin

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of Protestant
after re-forming, the letters of Latin appear in a new order

explanation.surface: A complaint about a Protestant leader using Latin after the Reformation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'post-Reformation' sounds historical but means Latin re-formed into LAINT, placed after P.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaint is a literary or legal word for a complaint or grievance.

clue.text: Time to put squeeze on 17?

parts.note: a hug is a squeeze

explanation.surface: It is time to put pressure on a criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 refers to the answer CRIMINAL at 17 down.
explanation.definitionFit: A thug is a violent lawbreaker, one kind of criminal.

clue.text: Point taken by smallest in litter? Nothing to be added to that

indicators.note: taken by says the point letter is absorbed into the runt phrase

parts.note: the runt is the weakest, smallest animal in a litter
E (east) is a compass point
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A tiny piglet gets the point; nothing more needs saying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nothing to be added to that' looks like a closing remark, but splits: O is added, and 'to that' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Thereunto is an archaic adverb meaning to that thing or place.

clue.text: Nader's contribution to moral philosophy

indicators.note: contribution to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An American activist adds to ethical thought.
explanation.walkthrough: Ralph Nader is an American consumer advocate and presidential candidate; the possessive in the definition matches the possessive sense of the hidden name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ralph is the first name of the activist Nader, a first name for a surname.

clue.text: Coin found by retired person in military base

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the soldier is read backwards

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier
the noble was an old English gold coin

explanation.surface: Money is discovered by a retired soldier at an army camp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'military base' looks like a single phrase, but 'base' alone is the definition. The NOBLE was a medieval English gold coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignoble and base both describe dishonourable, mean conduct; they are synonyms.

clue.text: Taking nothing in, beginning to feel a pain

indicators.note: beginning to means the first letter of feel

parts.note: a sting is a sharp pain

explanation.surface: Eating nothing, one starts to feel a pang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking nothing in' sounds like not understanding, but means not eating.
explanation.definitionFit: Fasting is abstaining from food, consuming nothing.

clue.text: Roller with order for Rover

parts.note: heel is the command telling a dog (Rover) to walk close

explanation.surface: A steamroller comes with a command for a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: Rover is a stock name for a dog, so its order is HEEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheel is something that rolls, a roller in a general sense.

clue.text: Desperate to get 21 down? Ha-ha!

parts.note: the answer to 21 down means bear or survive, as does last
a ha-ha is a sunken ditch serving as a fence in a landscaped garden

explanation.surface: Someone frantic about survival is greeted with laughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ha-ha' looks like laughter, but a ha-ha is a sunk fence or ditch on British country estates.
explanation.definitionFit: A last-ditch effort is a desperate final attempt.

clue.text: One given top billing in England? I'm a stranger!

indicators.note: stranger read as more strange means the letters are put in an odd order

explanation.surface: A celebrity in England protests that he is a foreigner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'm a stranger' looks like an introduction, but 'stranger' is the anagram signal on ENGLAND and I'M A.
explanation.definitionFit: The leading man is the male star, billed first on posters.

clue.text: Period in China, both useful and unpleasant

parts.note: handy means useful
nasty means unpleasant

explanation.surface: An era in Chinese history is described as practical yet horrid.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface split is misleading: the answer's own word break comes after the third letter, naming the Han rulers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Han dynasty ruled China from 206 BC to AD 220, a historical era.

clue.text: Palace official troubling monarch with "Dear Bill" letters

indicators.note: troubling suggests disturbing the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A court official upsets the sovereign with satirical letters from Private Eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dear Bill' letters were a Private Eye satire column; 'letters' hints that only their letters are used.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lord Chamberlain is the senior officer of the British royal household.

clue.text: Not the last resort in state for Capone, say

indicators.note: in says the trimmed resort sits inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: Cal is an abbreviation for California, a US state

indicators.note: not the last means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: Rimini is an Italian seaside resort

explanation.surface: A gangster ends up somewhere other than his final resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last resort' reads as an idiom, but 'Not the last' trims RIMINI to RIMIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Al Capone was a notorious gangster, an example of a criminal.

clue.text: This bean may be transformed into a drink

indicators.note: may be transformed says the letters can be rearranged

explanation.surface: A coffee bean might turn into a beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: Absinthe is a strong aniseed-flavoured spirit, an example of a drink.

clue.text: Support is in sink

indicators.note: in says the word is goes within the synonym

parts.note: to subside is to sink down

explanation.surface: A prop sits in the kitchen sink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sink' looks like a noun, but it is the verb SUBSIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To subsidise is to support financially.

clue.text: Orlando's flowers …

explanation.surface: The setter Orlando names his flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: Orlando Bloom is a film actor; the setter, also Orlando, plays on the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Orlando's surname gives the possessive, and blooms are blossoms, i.e. flowers.

clue.text: Try some Bacon or Lamb?

explanation.surface: Sample a little bacon or lamb.
explanation.walkthrough: Bacon and Lamb look like meats but are essayists Francis Bacon and Charles Lamb.
explanation.definitionFit: To essay means to attempt; essays were written by Francis Bacon and Charles Lamb.

clue.text: … complete with flower for bear

parts.note: to end is to complete
a flower is something that flows, a river; the Ure is a Yorkshire river

explanation.surface: Finishing with a bloom to stand for a bear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' means a river here; the Ure flows through Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: To endure is to tolerate or put up with, as to bear.

clue.text: Loving Gordian knots

indicators.note: knots, as a verb, says the letters get tangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is fond of the famously tangled knot.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoring means showing deep love, a synonym for loving.

clue.text: Freight heading off in legendary ship

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: cargo is freight

explanation.surface: Goods leave for a famous mythical vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The Argo was the ship of Jason and the Argonauts in Greek myth.

clue.text: Mary provides wonderful food when hosting party

indicators.note: hosting says the manna piece holds the party inside

parts.note: manna is the miraculous food from heaven
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Mary serves heavenly fare at a party she is throwing.
explanation.definitionFit: The Madonna is a title for Mary, mother of Jesus.

clue.text: Drink picked up for Darius?

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the word is taken by sound

parts.note: mead is a drink made from honey

explanation.surface: A drink is picked up for King Darius.
explanation.walkthrough: Darius the Mede appears in the Book of Daniel.
explanation.definitionFit: Darius the Mede is a biblical figure, an example of a man of Media.

clue.text: School master's third brightest star

parts.note: a gam is a school of whales
MA, Master of Arts, is a degree

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster's star pupil comes third.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School master' looks like a teacher; it is two pieces: GAM (a whale school) and MA.
explanation.definitionFit: Stars in a constellation are lettered in Greek, the third brightest usually getting this third letter.

clue.text: Slug behind tree in military base

indicators.note: behind says the slug piece comes after the tree

parts.note: the alder is a tree
a slug is a shot, of drink or a bullet

explanation.surface: A bullet lodges behind a tree at an army camp.
explanation.walkthrough: Aldershot is a Hampshire town known as the home of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: Aldershot is a garrison town in Hampshire, England, a major army base.
